title: With Pareus' definition of natural, the dispute is only about a word
source_text: XXIX. Verum quaestio ista solum est de nomine, respectu eorum qui inter Protestantes naturale cum Paraeo definiunt, Id sine quo natura in suis principiis non fuit primitus condita. Hoc enim sensu fatentur, ut vidimus, Doctores Scholae Romanae immortalitatem fuisse primo homini naturalem.
pass_a_gloss: But that question is only about the name, in respect of those among the Protestants who define natural with Pareus, That without which nature in its principles was not first founded. For in this sense, as we have seen, the Doctors of the Roman School confess that immortality was natural to the first man.
pass_b_english: But for those Protestants who define "natural" with Pareus as "that without which nature was not first made in its principles," the question is only about a word. For in that sense, as we have seen, the teachers of the Roman school admit that immortality was natural to the first man.

choices.why: Le Blanc means a verbal, not real, disagreement; that contrast is picked up in the next thesis.
rejected: is about a name only, not a reality
